ruling.recommended_action: Route to Ryde human safety review (RydeHELP); attach fact summary F1–F7; no refund action. Note 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths to the rider. No account action at this stage.
ruling.escalation_reason: Rider alleges dangerous driving (speeding, hard braking, shoulder overtaking) on trip 21:22–21:34, Jurong East MRT → NUS [F5]. No telematics in the fact table: F1 gives distance only (8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal), F2 duration only (12.8 min vs 14 min estimate). Chat is pickup logistics only [F3][F4]; driver denies in F5. Dispatch to Ryde human safety review under SAFE-2; note 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths. Check: speed/harsh-driving exceptions for the trip window; driver statement F5; credibility profiles F6/F7 (non-decisive).

rejected_claims.reason: F2 (12.8 min vs 14 min estimate) with no detour [F1] is a single-fact 1.0 min difference that is equally consistent with light traffic or a favourable light cycle and is not a speed measurement; it cannot be read as corroboration of sustained speeding [F1][F2][SAFE-2]. It is recorded only as a neutral fact for the human reviewer.

Correct as far as it goes — no refund head exists on a fixed-quote RydeX fare with no excess distance [F1][FARE-1][RD-2] — but it is not a claim in the rider's favour and does not affect the escalation outcome [F1][FARE-1].

Accepted on routing: F1 shows 8.5 km actual vs 8.6 km optimal with no off-route segment [F1][RD-1]. It does not answer the rider's case, which is the manner of driving, and no RD-2 refund attaches [F1][RD-1][RD-2].

Reading F2 as evidence of lawful driving is rejected: a 12.8 min run against a 14 min estimate is equally explained by traffic or light cycles and is not a speed or behaviour measurement [F1][F2][SAFE-2].
The driver's clean 90-day record [F7] is a profile fact; profiles never decide a case alone and RD-6 governs repeated route violations, not a dangerous-driving escalation [F7][RD-6][SAFE-2].

The driver's statement that the rider never complained [F5] is user-submitted and cannot defeat the rider's first-hand safety account; silence on safety in the chat [F3][F4] is not evidence of safety [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2].

Accepted that SAFE-1 is not engaged — the messages are neutral logistics [F3][F4] — but this does not remove the SAFE-2 escalation ground, which needs only an allegation of dangerous driving [F3][F4][SAFE-2].
